title: Optimization of overlap extension PCR for efficient transgene construction
author: Hilgarth, Lanigan

The purpose of the Overlap PCR reaction is to generate the full-length fusion gene containing the P2A site from the two primary fragments generated in Step 1. This PCR reaction does not use any primers and relies on the overlapping sequences generated in Step 1 for primer extension. It is important that both primary fragments be present in the PCR reaction in equimolar amounts. We generally use ∼100 ng/1 kb fragment in the PCR reaction. Calculation of molar ratios may be done using a biomath calculator such as NEBioCalculator (https://nebiocalculator.neb.com/#!/ligation). The overlap PCR reactions were carried out in a volume of 50 μL. P2A fusions with fluorophores can be GC rich. To streamline the process, we recommend setting up two PCR reactions, one with GC enhancer and one without, and do the same for step 3: final fusion gene PCR amplification. steps.title: Gather equipment and supplies
steps.instruction: Collect a PCR thermal cycler, PCR tubes, sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, benchtop microcentrifuge, agarose gel electrophoresis apparatus, gel documentation system, adjustable micropipettors (0.1–1000 µL), aerosol‑resistant tips, Phusion and Q5 DNA polymerases, 10 mM dNTP mix, 10X TAE buffer, agarose, primers, Monarch® DNA gel extraction kit, restriction enzymes, T4 DNA ligase, and a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Prepare PCR reagents
steps.instruction: Thaw and keep on ice the 5X Q5 reaction buffer, 10 mM dNTP mix, Q5 GC enhancer (if used), Q5 DNA polymerase, Phusion DNA polymerase (optional), and molecular‑grade water. Aliquot primers at 10 µM stock concentration.

steps.title: Design primers for P2A fusion
steps.instruction: Design reverse primer 1‑P2A for CDS1 and forward primer 2‑P2A for CDS2 so that each carries a 36 bp P2A overlap (Tm ≈ 65 °C) at the 5′ end and gene‑specific sequence (Tm ≈ 62 °C) at the 3′ end; include restriction sites in primers R1 and R2. Ensure CDS1 has a Kozak sequence before ATG, no stop codon, and is in‑frame with the P2A cassette; the only stop codon will be at the end of CDS2.

steps.title: Amplify primary fragments (Step 1)
steps.instruction: Set up two 50 µL Q5 PCR reactions (one for CDS1, one for CDS2) on ice: 10 µL 5X Q5 buffer, 1 µL 10 mM dNTP, 3 µL 10 µM primer mix (R1 + 1‑P2A for CDS1; R2 + 2‑P2A for CDS2), 10 ng template DNA, and water to 50 µL. If a GC‑rich template requires enhancer, replace 10 µL water with 10 µL 5X Q5 GC enhancer. Optionally substitute Q5 with Phusion polymerase. Run touchdown PCR: 94 °C 30 s (1 cycle); 94 °C 15 s, 67 °C (decrease 0.5 °C per cycle) 15 s, 72 °C 30 s per kb for 17 cycles; then 94 °C 15 s, 59 °C 15 s, 72 °C 30 s per kb for 23 cycles; 72 °C 2 min (1 cycle); hold 10 °C. Analyze 30 µL of each reaction on a 1 % agarose TAE gel containing 1X Gel Red at 10 V/cm for 30 min, visualize under UV, excise bands of expected size, and purify DNA with the Monarch® gel extraction kit eluting in 30 µL buffer. Quantify purified fragments with a Nanodrop and store at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR mix for each fragment on ice.
Add GC enhancer if needed (replace 10 µL water with 10 µL enhancer).
Run the described touchdown thermocycling program.
Run 30 µL of each reaction on a 1 % agarose gel with Gel Red, run 10 V/cm for 30 min.
Excise correct bands, perform gel extraction with Monarch kit, elute in 30 µL.
Measure DNA concentration with Nanodrop and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Overlap PCR to fuse fragments (Step 2)
steps.instruction: In a 50 µL reaction combine 10 µL 5X Q5 buffer, 2 µL 10 mM dNTP, 0.5 µL Q5 polymerase, and equimolar amounts of Primary Fragment 1 and Primary Fragment 2 (≈ 100 ng per kb of each fragment). For a GC‑enhanced version add 10 µL 5X Q5 GC enhancer and reduce water accordingly. Run touchdown PCR: 94 °C 30 s (1 cycle); 94 °C 15 s, 72 °C (decrease 0.5 °C per cycle) 30 s per kb for 9 cycles; 94 °C 15 s, 67.5 °C (decrease 0.5 °C per cycle) 15 s, 72 °C 30 s per kb for 5 cycles; 72 °C 2 min (1 cycle); hold 10 °C. No cleanup is required; store the overlap PCR product at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the overlap PCR mix (with or without GC enhancer).
Run the specified touchdown thermocycling program.

steps.title: Final fusion PCR amplification (Step 3)
steps.instruction: Set up a 50 µL Q5 PCR using low primer concentrations (1–2.5 µM): 10 µL 5X Q5 buffer, 2 µL 10 mM dNTP, 4 µL Step 2 PCR product as template, 1 µL primer 1 (R1) and 1 µL primer 2 (R2) from Step 1, 0.5 µL Q5 polymerase, and water to 50 µL. For a GC‑enhanced reaction also add 10 µL 5X Q5 GC enhancer. Run touchdown PCR: 94 °C 30 s (1 cycle); 94 °C 15 s, 67 °C (decrease 0.5 °C per cycle) 15 s, 72 °C 30 s per kb for 17 cycles; 94 °C 15 s, 59 °C 15 s, 72 °C 30 s per kb for 23 cycles; 72 °C 2 min (1 cycle); hold 10 °C. Analyze 30 µL on a 1 % agarose TAE gel with 1X Gel Red at 10 V/cm for 30 min, UV‑visualize, excise the correctly sized full‑length band, and purify with the Monarch® kit eluting in 30 µL. The purified product can be digested with the restriction sites introduced by primers R1 and R2, ligated into the expression vector, transformed, and sequenced to confirm the construct.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the final PCR mix with low‑concentration primers (with or without GC enhancer).
Run the described touchdown thermocycling program.
Run 30 µL of the reaction on a 1 % agarose gel with Gel Red, run 10 V/cm for 30 min, visualize under UV, and excise the correct band.
Purify the gel slice with the Monarch® kit, eluting in 30 µL.
Digest the purified product with the 5′ and 3′ restriction enzymes, ligate into the expression vector, transform, and sequence to verify.
